Its dimension_vector [0,1,-1,0,0,0,0] (SI: L T^-1) supplies the L and T exponents that match every known coordinate of the submitted vector. Therefore the candidate exponents exactly represent the physical meaning of U_inf in the original problem.

The variable nu in the problem denotes the kinematic viscosity. KB record pq_kinematic_viscosity defines ν as dynamic viscosity divided by density, lists the symbol nu/ν, gives SI unit m^2 s^-1 and dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0] (L^2 T^-1). This record directly corresponds to the intended physical quantity in the problem and supports all provided exponent coordinates.

The ledger defines MKE as the integral ∫_0^delta U^2 dy. KB record pq_integrated_velocity_squared explicitly defines the 'integrated mean-flow squared-velocity measure' as integral U^2 dy and provides the SI dimension L^3 T^-2 (dimension_vector [0,3,-2,0,0,0,0]). That record therefore defines the same integral quantity named MKE in the problem and supplies the exact exponents for all known base dimensions.

The ledger's 'delta' is the boundary-layer thickness at 99% of U_inf. KB record pq_boundary_layer_thickness has canonical_quantity 'boundary-layer thickness' and explicitly lists the 99%-definition as an operational choice; its SI dimension is L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). This record matches the variable's meaning and supports the provided spatial exponent.

KB record pq_displacement_thickness provides that same canonical definition and lists SI dimension L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). The record therefore applies directly to the ledger entry and supports the spatial exponent in the candidate vector.

The ledger labels theta as the boundary-layer momentum thickness (∫_0^delta (U/U_inf)(1 - U/U_inf) dy). KB record pq_momentum_thickness has canonical_quantity 'momentum thickness' with that definition and SI dimension L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). Although 'theta' can denote other quantities (e.g., an angle), the original problem text explicitly names momentum thickness, so pq_momentum_thickness correctly applies and supplies the spatial exponent.
